title: Preserve missing values through Styler gradient normalization
answers: Why do missing cells get the lowest gradient color when all valid values are equal?
How should background_gradient and text_gradient color NaN cells?
How do I preserve a colormap's custom bad color when vmin equals vmax?
body:
Symptom: Missing cells receive the lowest colormap color in background_gradient or text_gradient when all valid values are equal.
Root cause: pandas/io/formats/style.py:_background_gradient uses matplotlib Normalize, which maps NaN to zero when vmin == vmax.
Fix pattern: Restore NaN using the original gmap's missing-value mask after normalization, then pass the preserved result to both default and explicitly supplied colormaps so their missing-value color is respected.
Constraints: Both gradient methods must preserve missing-value coloring whether equal bounds arise from the data or explicit vmin/vmax; valid values must retain their normalized colors.
Regression coverage: pandas/tests/io/formats/style/test_matplotlib.py:test_background_gradient_nan_single_value checks both methods and implicit/explicit equal bounds, comparing missing-cell styles across constant and varying columns and against valid cells.
applies: Styler background_gradient and text_gradient changes involving normalization or colormap application.
